This means that for any integer \( x \) in the array, you would use \( |x| \), where \( |x| \) denotes the non-negative value of \( x \). For example, the magnitude of -4 is 4, and the magnitude of 4 is also 4.

The "product of all signs" in this problem refers to multiplying together the signs of each number in the array. Each non-zero integer has a sign: 1 for positive numbers and -1 for negative numbers. Zero is typically considered as 0. So, for an array like [1, 2, 2, -4], the signs would be [1, 1, 1, -1], and their product is \(1 \times 1 \times 1 \times (-1) = -1\). This product is then multiplied by the sum of the magnitudes of the integers in the array to get the final result.

Yes, the product of all signs being 1, -1, or 0 refers to the product of the sign function applied to each element in the array.
